input_schema.description:
Reads one item: the `timeline.get` item summary plus its track, source, audio and visual
properties. `fields` limits the extra sections (`name`, `source`, `audio`, `visual`).

fields.description: Sections to include: any of `name`, `source`, `audio`, `visual` (default all).

input_schema.title: ItemGet

queries.name: item.get

attached_to.description: The item this one is attached to (it follows that parent), if any.

fade_in.description:
Fade from silence at the start of the clip (WP-2E.01). Absent in documents written
before it: no fade.

oneOf.description: Gain rises in a straight line (the default).
Gain rises quickly then flattens (`log10(1 + 9x)`): a fast, natural-sounding fade in.
Constant power with a matching fade of the same shape on the other clip: `sin(x*pi/2)`.
Gentle at both ends: `(1 - cos(x*pi)) / 2`.

fade_out.description: Fade to silence at the end of the clip (WP-2E.01). Absent in older documents: no fade.

items.description: A key: a value at an item-relative time (flicks), and the easing of the segment to the next key (keyframes §3.1).

interp.description:
How the segment that starts at a key moves to the next key (keyframes §4). It is a closed
set: a new kind is a schema change.

Every kind except `hold` is an easing `p(u)` with `p(0) = 0` and `p(u) → 1` as `u → 1`,
fed into one lerp per value type (§5). On the wire it is an object tagged by `kind`
(`{"kind": "bezier", "x1": 0.42, "y1": 0, "x2": 0.58, "y2": 1, "preset": "ease_in_out"}`)
with exactly its fields; construction checks their ranges (KF-5) and the hint (KF-7).

oneOf.description: The key's value until the next key, then a jump (§4.2).

A CSS-style cubic Bézier from (0, 0) to (1, 1), normalized to the segment (§4.4).
(`x1`, `y1`) shapes the speed leaving the key, (`x2`, `y2`) the speed arriving at the
next one.

at_source.description: The media position of the frame shown.

speed.description: Playback speed, an exact fraction (`{"num": 1, "den": 2}` is half speed).

blend_mode.description: How the item combines with what is below.

crop.description: Edges of the source picture cut away.

bottom.description: Fraction removed from the bottom edge.

input_schema.description:
Reads a sequence in layers: `depth` 0 is the sequence summary, 1 adds its tracks (summaries
only, small), 2 adds the items. `fields` limits the sections returned (`name`, `format`,
`duration`, `tracks`); the id and the counts are always included and always describe the
whole sequence. At depth 2, `range` lists only the items that overlap `[from, to)`, and
`limit` pages them in track order, then start order: `next_cursor` is the `cursor` of the
next page (absent on the last one). A long timeline is best read as the depth 1 overview,
then depth 2 pages of the part that matters.

fields.description: Sections to include: any of `name`, `format`, `duration`, `tracks` (default all).

limit.description: Depth 2: most items to list, `1..=1000` (default: all); see `next_cursor`.

range.description: Depth 2: list only the items that overlap `{from, to}` (flicks, "2.5s" or "f:60").

anyOf.description: A time: integer flicks (1/705600000 s), or a string: seconds ("62.5s"), a frame ("f:1500") or a timecode ("00:01:02:03", drop-frame "00:01:02;03"). Frames and timecodes use the frame rate of the target's sequence.

picture shows, the color does.

dim.description: How much of the blurred picture's light is taken away, `0..=1` (0: none, 1: black).
